title: 17-DMAG ameliorates neuroinflammation and BBB disruption via SOX5 mediated PI3K/Akt pathway after intracerebral hemorrhage in rats.
authors: Hu, Di; Mo, Xiaocong; Luo, Jihang; Wang, Fang; Huang, Cheng; Xie, Hesong; Jin, Ling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究17-DMAG通过SOX5/PI3K/Akt通路改善脑出血后神经炎症和血脑屏障损伤，属于疾病机制与药物研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) can result in secondary brain injury due to inflammation and breakdown of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which are closely associated with patient prognosis. The potential of the heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) inhibitor 17-DMAG in promoting neuroprotection has been observed in certain vascular diseases. However, the precise role of 17-DMAG treatment in ICH is not yet fully understood. In this study, we found that treatment with 17-DMAG (5 mg/kg) effectively reduced hematoma expansion and resulted in improved neurological outcomes. Meanwhile, the injection of 17-DMAG had a positive effect on reducing BBB disruption in rats with ICH. This effect was achieved by increasing the levels of BBB tight junction proteins (TJPs) such as zo-1, claudin-5, and occludin. As a result, the leakage of EB extravasation, brain edema and IgG in the peri-hematoma tissue were reduced. Furthermore, the injection of 17-DMAG decreased the infiltration of neutrophils into the brain tissues surrounding the hematoma in ICH rats and also reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-alpha. Next, we used integrative mass spectrometry (MS) and molecular docking analysis to confirm that sex determining region Y-box protein 5 (SOX5) is a potential direct target of 17-DMAG in ICH. SOX5 encodes a positive regulator of the PI3K/Akt axis, and treatment with 17-DMAG resulted in a noticeable increase in SOX5 accumulation. To further investigate the role of SOX5, we employed virus-regulated SOX5 silencing and found that suppressing SOX5 blocked the ability of 17-DMAG to suppress neutrophil trafficking. Additionally, silencing SOX5 blocked the protective effects of 17-DMAG on the BBB by inhibiting PI3K, p-Akt, and BBB TJPs levels, which led to an increase in EB and IgG leakage in the peri-hematoma tissue after ICH. Similarly, when SOX5 was knocked down, the protective effects of 17-DMAG were lost. Overall, the results of our study indicate that the injection of 17-DMAG has the potential to mitigate neuroinflammation and prevent the disruption of the BBB caused by ICH, resulting in improved neurological outcomes in rats. These positive effects are attributed to the regulation of SOX5 and activation of the PI3K/Akt pathway. These findings highlight the possibility of targeting SOX5 and the PI3K/Akt pathway as a novel therapeutic approach for ICH.
abstract_zh: 脑出血（ICH）可因炎症及血脑屏障（BBB）的破坏而导致继发性脑损伤，这些过程与患者预后密切相关。热休克蛋白90（Hsp90）抑制剂17-DMAG在促进神经保护方面的潜力已在某些血管疾病中被观察到。然而，17-DMAG治疗在ICH中的确切作用尚未完全明了。在本研究中，我们发现，使用17-DMAG（5 mg/kg）治疗能有效减少血肿扩大，并改善神经功能结局。同时，注射17-DMAG对减轻ICH大鼠的BBB破坏具有积极作用。这一效果是通过提高BBB紧密连接蛋白（TJPs）如zo-1、claudin-5和occludin的水平来实现的。因此，血肿周围组织中EB外渗、脑水肿及IgG的渗漏均有所减少。此外，注射17-DMAG降低了ICH大鼠血肿周围脑组织中中性粒细胞的浸润，并减少了促炎细胞因子IL-6和TNF-α的产生。接下来，我们采用整合质谱（MS）和分子对接分析，确认性别决定区Y-box蛋白5（SOX5）是17-DMAG在ICH中的潜在直接靶点。SOX5编码PI3K/Akt轴的正调控因子，而17-DMAG治疗导致SOX5积累显著增加。为进一步探讨SOX5的作用，我们采用病毒调控的SOX5沉默，发现抑制SOX5会阻断17-DMAG抑制中性粒细胞迁移的能力。此外，沉默SOX5通过抑制PI3K、p-Akt及BBB TJPs水平，阻断了17-DMAG对BBB的保护作用，导致ICH后血肿周围组织中EB和IgG渗漏增加。同样，当SOX5被敲低时，17-DMAG的保护效应丧失。总体而言，我们的研究结果表明，注射17-DMAG具有减轻神经炎症并防止ICH引起的BBB破坏的潜力，从而改善大鼠的神经功能结局。这些积极效应归因于对SOX5的调控及PI3K/Akt通路的激活。这些发现强调了将SOX5及PI3K/Akt通路作为ICH新型治疗靶点的可能性。
